title: Property taxes
prompt: What should Iowa do about property taxes?
context: Property taxes are what you pay each year on a home or land. They pay for local things like roads, police, fire departments, and schools. Iowa recently passed a law that limits how fast most city and county property taxes can grow and gives homeowners a tax break.
learnMore: The new law is SF 2472. It caps yearly growth in most city and county property taxes at 2% and takes 10% of a home's value off its taxable value (at least $5,500 and at most $20,000).

options.label: Get rid of them on homes
options.description: Phase out property taxes on people's homes completely over time.

options.label: Cut them more
options.description: Lower property taxes more, even if cities and counties have to cut some spending.

options.label: Cut them, but protect local services
options.description: Lower property taxes, but make sure things like police, fire, and roads keep their funding.

options.label: Wait and see
options.description: Leave the new law alone for now and see how it works before changing anything.

options.label: Let local governments decide
options.description: Give cities and counties more freedom to decide how to pay for their services.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate addressed the levy cap rate, its exceptions, the EMS levy, or the state backfill.

title: State income taxes and government spending
prompt: What should Iowa do with the state income tax?
context: The state income tax comes out of your paycheck. Iowa recently cut it to one rate for everyone: 3.8%. Lower taxes leave more money in your pocket, but also less money for state services.

options.label: Get rid of it over time
options.description: Lower the income tax step by step until it's gone, and cut state spending to make up for it.

options.label: Cut it more, but keep it
options.description: Lower the rate further, but don't get rid of the income tax.

options.label: Keep it at 3.8%
options.description: Keep the income tax where it is now.

options.label: No more cuts for now
options.description: Don't cut it any further until the state budget is balanced.

options.label: Raise it for high earners
options.description: Have people who make the most money pay a higher rate.

unansweredQuestions: SJR 11: no documented position for either candidate.
Neither candidate has a plan for the FY2027 budget gap.

title: Cost of living and housing affordability
prompt: What's the best way to make homes more affordable in Iowa?
context: Buying or renting a home costs more than it used to. Ideas include building more homes, limiting big investors, and helping first-time buyers.

options.label: Build more homes
options.description: Change local rules so more kinds of homes, like duplexes and small backyard houses, can be built.

options.label: Limit big investors
options.description: Stop large investment companies from buying up houses.

options.label: Help first-time buyers
options.description: Give first-time buyers help with their down payment.

options.label: Let the market handle it
options.description: Keep government mostly out of it and let builders and buyers sort it out.

title: Farm profitability and agricultural policy
prompt: What should Iowa do first to help farmers make a living?
context: What farmers earn depends on what they pay for seed, fertilizer, and equipment, what land costs, and how much they can sell to other countries.

options.label: Go after big farm-supply companies
options.description: Use laws against monopolies on the large companies that sell farmers seed, fertilizer, and equipment.

options.label: Limit who can buy farmland
options.description: Stop outside investors and big corporations from buying up Iowa farmland.

options.label: Push for open trade
options.description: Press the federal government to lower tariffs (taxes on imports and exports) so farmers can sell more overseas.

options.label: Stay out of it
options.description: Keep the state's role small and let the market decide.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate named Iowa Code ch. 9H or 10B, or explained how land confiscation or antitrust suits would work legally.

title: Eminent domain and landowner protections
prompt: Should landowners be forced to sell their land for a project that mainly helps a private company?
context: “Eminent domain” lets the government make someone sell their land for a public project, like a road, as long as they're paid for it. In Iowa, people have argued about using it for privately owned projects, like carbon dioxide (CO2) pipelines.
learnMore: Being against something in general is not the same as backing a specific bill. Both candidates have said they oppose taking land for private gain. Neither has said whether he would sign HF 2104, a bill on this issue.

options.label: No, never
options.description: Don't allow it when the project mainly benefits a private company.

options.label: Only with stricter rules
options.description: Allow it only with tougher rules and better pay for landowners.

options.label: Decide case by case
options.description: Keep the current law and let state regulators decide each project.

options.label: Yes, if it benefits the public
options.description: Allow it for private projects that bring public benefits like jobs or lower energy costs, as long as owners are paid.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate said whether he would sign HF 2104.
Neither addressed the Utilities Commission, Summit's permit, or IUC appointment criteria.

title: Drinking water, nitrates, and environmental regulation
prompt: What's the best way to keep farm runoff out of Iowa's drinking water?
context: Fertilizer from farm fields can wash into rivers and wells. At high levels, a chemical from it called nitrate can make drinking water unsafe. Right now, Iowa mostly relies on farmers taking voluntary steps.

options.label: Pay farmers to help
options.description: Give farmers more money and tax breaks for practices that reduce runoff.

options.label: Set rules farmers must follow
options.description: Set limits on farm runoff that farmers are required to meet.

options.label: Test the water more
options.description: Test water more often and warn people when it isn't safe.

options.label: Keep things as they are
options.description: Keep the current voluntary approach.

unansweredQuestions: Neither candidate addressed HF 2771 water treatment funding or Iowa Flood Center funding.
